_: EVIDENCE CARDS — Sentinel Report. Every card is a FILED FACT with the command that produced it and the URL that verifies it. status GREEN = a filing says it. AMBER = a filing implies it and a second source is needed. Nothing here is characterisation. Cards feed OpenMontage scenes; the `line` is what goes on screen, the `caveat` is what must go on screen WITH it.
rules: A card with a caveat may not be used without its caveat.
A FLOOR is never presented as a total. A CEILING is never presented as a floor.
Verify every figure against `verify` before it goes on screen.
status AMBER does not go on screen at all.

cards.subject: Ohio Flyer PAC
cards.line: One committee. Two candidates. Both Ohio Senate seats. Opposite directions.
cards.detail: $4,459,869 total. $3,342,670 AGAINST Sherrod Brown. $1,117,199 FOR Jon Husted. The two sum to the total exactly — there is no third candidate.
cards.caveat: Concentration is not intent. A state-focused committee is single-state by design.

cards.subject: Ohio Flyer PAC donors
cards.line: One donor is 35% of the committee.
cards.detail: A PUBLIC VOCIE, INC. (sic, as filed) gave $1,000,000 of $2,834,231 in reported receipts. Coverage 100% — this is a share of essentially all its money.
cards.caveat: The company found in the registry is in COLUMBUS; the FEC filing says WEST CHESTER. SAME-ENTITY IS NOT CONFIRMED.

cards.subject: TEAM HUSTED joint fundraiser
cards.line: $8,253,532 split five ways. 63% to the campaign. 7% to the super PAC.
cards.detail: HUSTED FOR SENATE $5,215,998 (63.2%) · NRSC $1,129,393 · JOBS OPPORTUNITY NOW PAC $824,033 · OHIO FLYER PAC $604,861 (7.3%) · Ohio Republican Party $479,247. The five account for the 24G total exactly.
cards.caveat: A transfer is not a gift and not an endorsement. Whether a super PAC may participate in a candidate JFC is a question of FEC rules and advisory opinions this desk has NOT answered. Nothing here asserts a violation.

cards.subject: Jobs Opportunity Now PAC
cards.line: The leadership PAC is Husted's. The register says so.
cards.detail: C00896688, Leadership PAC, first filed 2025-01-27, sponsor: HUSTED, JON (S6OH00304). 65.2% of its $1,263,717 came from TEAM HUSTED.
cards.caveat: A filed sponsor, not an inference from the name.

cards.subject: Jobs Opportunity Now PAC spending
cards.line: It paid the caucus: twenty Senate campaigns, $10,000 each.
cards.detail: $424,500 in 68 contributions across twenty states, plus $105,000 to HUSTED VICTORY and $15,000 to the NRSC. No independent expenditures at all.
cards.caveat: This is the TEXTBOOK function of a leadership PAC. A figure at the cap describes the cap, not the giver.

cards.subject: HUSTED VICTORY
cards.line: Raised $3.6 million. Sent 76 cents of every dollar to one media firm.
cards.detail: $3,636,779 raised (coverage 100%, 85 donors). $2,755,532 to SRCP MEDIA INC. — 75.8% of everything raised. $28,461 transferred to participants — 0.78%.
cards.caveat: A joint fundraiser legitimately pays the COST of raising money and allocates it among participants. 'MEDIA' does not say whether this is fundraising solicitation or campaign advertising, and the purpose code cannot distinguish them. THIS IS A QUESTION, NOT A FINDING.

cards.subject: Sherrod Brown 2026
cards.line: Six committees produced every dollar of the $13.5m spent against him.
cards.detail: $13,471,230 against in 91 expenditures; $1,340,363 for in 69. Contested ratio 0.10. AFP Action $4,888,349 · SLF PAC $4,508,418 · Ohio Flyer PAC $3,342,670 · America PAC $648,371 · Conservative Caucus $73,419 · Red Senate $10,002. The six are the total, to within a dollar.
cards.caveat: Schedule E complete (3 of 25 pages). Money IN is TRUNCATED at the 2,500-row cap, so OUTSIDE PRESSURE 15.70x is a CEILING — the true multiple is lower.

cards.subject: Jon Husted 2026
cards.line: WITHDRAWN — 40.19x was wrong by a factor of 18 to 30.
cards.detail: The published figure divided $19.1m of outside money by $475,873 — a TRUNCATED Schedule A sample, not the committee total. His committee reported $14,350,624 in receipts. Corrected: OUTSIDE PRESSURE 1.35x on receipts, 2.24x excluding the $5,675,891 of transfers in.
cards.caveat: DO NOT USE. Kept as a retraction, not a fact. The correct figure is in DELEG-01. This is what a ceiling looks like when it is not checked.

cards.subject: Wasserman Schultz, FL-25
cards.line: For every dollar spent attacking her, less than half a cent defended her.
cards.detail: 2024: $98,905 against in 46 expenditures, $395 for in 2. A ratio of 250:1. Contested ratio 0.00.
cards.caveat: The SMALLER ratio is often the larger operation — Brown is 10:1 on $13.5m, which is 136x this money. A ratio describes balance, not size.

cards.subject: AIPAC's own funds vs its conduit
cards.line: The number everyone reports is the one that carries no information.
cards.detail: AIPAC's PAC gave exactly $10,000 — the maximum — to Wasserman Schultz in 2022 AND 2024, to Miller, and to Brown. Four of four at the cap. The conduit column varies six-fold: $89,610 / $530,369 / $89,988 / $127,070.
cards.caveat: Conduit money is individuals' giving passing through, disclosed under their names. It is NEVER the organisation's donation.

cards.subject: EDF Action Votes
cards.line: An environmental committee that has never spent a dollar in support of anyone.
cards.detail: $5,759,827 in 2026, 100% opposition, two candidates only — Rogers $3,256,161 and Husted $2,503,666.
cards.caveat: Two targets is above the 5-row/$1,000 floor, so the arithmetic is not deciding this. But a committee formed late has one race left.

cards.subject: method
cards.line: We retired our own best finding.
cards.detail: §9 recorded three committees converging on Rogers and Husted. Reading the side split showed two of them were on OPPOSITE sides of all 8 candidates they shared — and Husted's leadership PAC funds six of the same names. It was the 2026 battleground map, not a network.
cards.caveat: The wrong reading is kept in the file with the retraction attached. Correcting it in place would hide the method that caught it.
cards.command: bin/sentinel connect asymmetry "Americans for Prosperity Action" --cycle 2026

cards.subject: Ohio's federal delegation, 2026
cards.line: Sixteen members raised $47.4 million. Two in five dollars came from PACs.
cards.detail: $47,405,708 raised across 16 seats; $14,582,896 — 39.5% — from political committees. PAC share ranges from 13.9% (Jordan) to 74.2% (Beatty), a five-fold spread that does not sort by party.
cards.caveat: PAC share is measured against CONTRIBUTIONS — individuals plus committees plus party — never against receipts, which include loans and transfers and would flatter anyone who lent their campaign money. Delegation totals are a sum of separate committees; nobody controls them jointly.

cards.subject: Contested Ohio seats, 2026
cards.line: Three of sixteen Ohio seats had money spent against them. One was attacked with nothing spent in its defence.
cards.detail: HUSTED $12,146,701 for / $7,270,291 against (1.67). KAPTUR $222,240 for / $706,277 against (0.31). MILLER $0 for / $423,010 against (0.00) — attacked and undefended. The other thirteen had nothing spent against them at all.
cards.caveat: A dot is not a safe seat — it means nobody spent against them, which is a different fact. Ratio is for-money over against-money.

cards.subject: Shared vendors, Husted-adjacent committees
cards.line: Four committees. The same small firms paid by all of them.
cards.detail: SOCKO STRATEGIES is paid by all four ($479,017). QUINTUS LLC by three ($596,562). IRONCLAD CONSULTING by two ($225,127). Ohio Flyer PAC — the independent-expenditure-only committee — shares three vendors with TEAM HUSTED, the candidate's own joint fundraiser.
cards.caveat: A shared vendor is a CONTRACT, stronger than a shared bill — but NOT evidence of coordination, and the payee data WEAKENS that reading. NOT ONE MEDIA FIRM IS SHARED: Ohio Flyer paid Strategic Media Placement, Majority Strategies and Strategy Group; Husted Victory paid SRCP Media; no overlap. What IS shared is back office — Anedot (payments), Broghamer (compliance) — plus three UNIDENTIFIED firms. That is what a firewall looks like from outside. FEC rules address common vendors directly, incl. the firewall safe harbour at 11 CFR 109.21(h). Nothing establishes a firewall was absent or required.

cards.subject: Ohio Flyer PAC — who placed the advertising
cards.line: Two operations, two vendors: the attack money and the support money went to different firms.
cards.detail: $3,244,873 to STRATEGIC MEDIA PLACEMENT INC. and $97,797 to THE STRATEGY GROUP FOR MEDIA — all against Sherrod Brown. $1,117,199 to MAJORITY STRATEGIES — all for Jon Husted. The three sum to its $4,459,869 exactly. None is shared with any Husted committee.
cards.caveat: Schedule E payees, not Schedule B. This is the SEPARATION side of the vendor story and must be shown with VENDOR-01, never instead of it.

cards.subject: Who runs the committees
cards.line: Both sides hired a compliance professional and made him treasurer. They hired different ones.
cards.detail: TEAM HUSTED, HUSTED VICTORY and JOBS OPPORTUNITY NOW all name KEVIN BROGHAMER as treasurer — and pay BROGHAMER COMPLIANCE $49,334 for 'COMPLIANCE CONSULTING'. OHIO FLYER PAC names CHRIS MARSTON and pays ELECTION CFO $15,117. Separate treasurers, separate compliance vendors, separate media firms.
cards.caveat: A shared treasurer is routinely innocent — compliance firms supply them as a service. This result CONFIRMS separation rather than showing coordination. It does not answer whether a super PAC may participate in a candidate's joint fundraiser, which is a question of FEC rules. Nothing asserts a violation.
cards.command: bin/sentinel connect control C00896928 C00912865 C00937797 C00896688

cards.subject: method
cards.line: We spent the day trying to break our own best finding, and succeeded five times.
cards.detail: 40.19x became 1.35x. Three 'converging' committees turned out to be on opposite sides of all eight candidates they shared. Half a surveillance sweep was an unquoted query, not noise. Two bills did not exist. And the shared-vendor table was weakened by the payee table, then by the treasurer table.
cards.caveat: Every one was caught by dividing, or by reading the same figure from another register. None was caught by looking harder at the original number.
cards.command: bin/sentinel connect control C00896928 C00912865 C00937797 C00896688

open_questions.q: The $91,631 gap: Ohio Flyer's Schedule A says $513,230 from TEAM HUSTED; TEAM HUSTED's Schedule B says $604,861. Four rows on the Husted side.
open_questions.note: The Jobs Opportunity Now -> Husted Victory transfer reconciles to the dollar across the same two schedules, so the method works and this gap is specific.

open_questions.q: Who are TEAM HUSTED's declared participants, and what is the allocation formula?
Is HUSTED VICTORY's $2,755,532 of 'MEDIA' fundraising solicitation or campaign advertising?
Is A PUBLIC VOICE, INC. of Columbus the same entity as the FEC's 'A PUBLIC VOCIE, INC.' of West Chester?
open_questions.note: Different county, 100 miles apart. If it IS the same non-profit, the trail ends there BY LAW — a c4 does not disclose donors.

open_questions.q: Husted's and Brown's Schedule A both hit the page cap, making both OUTSIDE PRESSURE figures CEILINGS.
Four Senate victory committees file from NEWPORT, KENTUCKY. One compliance firm, or something else?
open_questions.note: HUSTED VICTORY, SUSAN COLLINS FOR MAINE, ASHLEY MOODY VICTORY COMMITTEE and PUT ALASKA FIRST all appear at Newport KY in the NRSC donor rows. Almost certainly one compliance firm's address — the Broghamer/Marston pattern at scale. Checkable.
